name: LeoMiniGames v0.7.4
body:
# LeoMiniGames v0.7.4

Unreleased development notes. No v0.7.4 package or device qualification is claimed by this file.

## Reliability

- Update checks preserve the newest request when synchronous state observers change channels, clear results or delete the service. Retired checks cannot create duplicate replies.
- Cancelling an update retires its state before abort callbacks run, so a replacement check retains its state and an observer can delete the service safely.
- Input callbacks preserve replacement action values and focus. Stale press/release notifications, reset batches and physical-key mappings cannot overwrite newer input.
- Mod download tickets retain the catalog's package digest and length. Legacy tickets may omit those fields, but cannot redefine them.
- Pending mod/theme ticket requests reject a changed catalog origin. Catalog/download URLs reject embedded credentials.
- Update guidance preserves native, Flatpak and mobile package choices instead of labeling every non-Maintenance installation portable.

## Release tooling

- Pending manual QA reports can be prepared from a small source-bound package manifest. Existing reports are preserved; the tool clears stale pass claims and does not invent device evidence.
- QA names follow the canonical version and manifest version mismatches are rejected.
- Publication verifies GitHub package evidence and includes device-test limitations. Manual 25-target QA is optional and strictly checked when supplied.
- Release API responses are read from files to avoid Linux environment-size limits, with regressions for oversized collections and existing public releases.

## Compatibility and validation

The game API remains 0.7. Raw RCC compatibility and existing data boundaries remain in place. The release kit stays at Qt 6.10.2; Qt 6.12 is tested separately on GitHub. HarmonyOS, YLPlugin/YLPkg and pixel-format work remain groundwork, without HAP support, new decoders or a new runtime format.

Prepared runtime changes passed GitHub CI and Qt 6.12 desktop tests at `1c803c9`; local Qt 6.11.1 regression checks also passed. This version bump and main integration require fresh GitHub results and a new exact-source artifact build before a v0.7.4 release. Compilation and automated tests do not establish physical-device behavior.

## Validation and device-test limits

Exact-source CI and the [release artifact build](https://github.com/YoungLionOrganization/LeoMiniGames/actions/runs/41221918528) passed for `3e85f539d66111a51c59fad5c8c4390527489afd`. All 39 public asset names, contents and SHA-256 values were validated.

| Target | GitHub runner environment | Automated package checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows-x86_64 | GitHub Windows X64; QtIFW CLI; previous-version metadata fixture | ZIP/Setup launch, fixture upgrade, modify, uninstall and data preservation passed |
| Windows-x86_64-AVX2 | GitHub Windows X64; QtIFW CLI; previous-version metadata fixture | ZIP/Setup launch, fixture upgrade, modify, uninstall and data preservation passed |
| Windows-ARM64 | GitHub Windows ARM64; QtIFW CLI; previous-version metadata fixture | ZIP/Setup launch, fixture upgrade, modify, uninstall and data preservation passed |
| macOS-arm64 | GitHub macOS 15.8.2 / arm64 | ZIP/DMG launch and signature checks passed; Gatekeeper status 3 |
| macOS-x86_64 | GitHub macOS 15.7.9 / x86_64 | ZIP/DMG launch and signature checks passed; Gatekeeper status 3 |
| macOS-universal | GitHub macOS 15.8.2 / arm64 | ZIP/DMG launch and signature checks passed; Gatekeeper status 3 |

- Linux Ubuntu portable installers, AppImages/tarballs, Debian/Fedora/Arch packages and both Flatpak architectures passed automated install/reinstall/uninstall and builtin-game launch checks on GitHub runners or containers.
- Android x86, x86_64 and universal APKs were installed/launched on emulators with a certificate-validated HTTPS catalog probe. ARM64/ARMv7 packages were built and inspected; physical ARM device behavior was not tested.
- macOS apps are ad-hoc signed, without Developer ID signing or notarization. Gatekeeper can reject these downloads. The universal bundle was launched only on its runner architecture; both slices were not independently launched by that job.
- iOS/iPadOS unsigned developer bundles were compiled only. They are excluded from public release assets and were not tested on signed physical devices.
- Physical-device touch/haptics, interactive sound output and credential-store persistence have not been qualified by these automated checks. No completed manual 25-target QA report is claimed.

name: LeoMiniGames v0.7.3
body:
# LeoMiniGames v0.7.3

This patch repairs the Android OpenSSL library dependency, explicitly extracts native TLS plugins and checks every packaged ABI's dependency closure and compiled manifest. Emulator evidence must include a certificate-validated HTTPS catalog request. Windows portable and installer payloads include the matching MSVC runtime DLLs.

Save files that fail loading are protected from automatic overwrite. Repeated unchanged saves preserve recovery backups. Session shutdown runs through one guarded lifecycle sequence, and external game migrations use the game's own JavaScript engine. Input handling uses native Qt key events, and builtin timers suspend while backgrounded.

Backup recovery validates migrations before changing files, and missing primaries with surviving backups remain protected until successfully loaded. Malformed catalog rows preserve the previous list. Resource filenames containing URL delimiters load correctly, and keyboard layout changes no longer leave native actions stuck.

Explicit save deletion handles protected slots and restores staged backups on failure. Invalid numeric service values no longer unlock achievements, accelerate timing or hold input; statistics avoid overflow and preserve full stores. Reentrant game transitions discard stale lifecycle/open notifications and retain replacement sessions.

Cancelled external QML loads cannot publish a late ready state or replace a newer session. Missing required root properties report a load error and retire the failed component.

Update actions require a newer validated version. Linux desktop updates open the release page for distribution and package-format selection instead of using a generic recommended binary.

Package updates preserve installed runtime metadata, reject incompatible candidates and restore the previous package if the installed index cannot be committed. Running game packages cannot be replaced or removed. Theme downloads verify package identity and version against the catalog.

Linux packages now include Debian DEBs, Fedora RPMs, an Arch pacman package, KDE Flatpak bundles and a portable user Setup.run installer alongside AppImage/tarballs. Automated Linux tests install, launch all six games, reinstall and uninstall, retaining user data. Android AVD creation is checked before launching the emulator; ARM64 CRT deployment filters files by PE architecture.

Failed Linux user-installer upgrades restore the previous payload and integration files. If rollback also fails, recovery files are retained and their location is reported.

The installation guide covers package selection, Arch/Flatpak, upgrading and removal, and is included in desktop payloads. Windows artifact jobs exercise portable/Setup launch and Maintenance Tool servicing on disposable runners, including an older-metadata upgrade fixture and optional-component modification. A separate GitHub lane checks Qt 6.12 desktop compatibility; the release kit remains Qt 6.10.2, and HarmonyOS is preparation for a later version.

Windows online upgrades register the installed component version instead of retaining the original Setup version. macOS packages are assembled before ad-hoc signing, and signature integrity is verified in both ZIP and DMG payloads; Developer ID signing and notarization remain separate.

Audio error handlers can stop or replace music safely. A newer nested music request retains ownership of playback instead of being overwritten by a retired request.

Interrupted save migrations and snapshot callbacks cannot populate another game's memory. Retired save notifications preserve the replacement session's pending changes.

Release validation checks the exact 39 asset names, archive contents, native dependency closure and remote sizes/digests. API compatibility remains 0.7; all six built-in games use native lifecycle hooks and atomic state persistence; boards, hands, flags and active time resume, while Reaction Tap restarts active timing rounds. Publication uses successful GitHub tests and source-bound package evidence, with physical-device limitations disclosed below. A manual QA report is optional and must match the exact candidate when supplied. The historical backend companion has not been deployed by this patch.

name: LeoMiniGames v0.7.2
body:
# LeoMiniGames v0.7.2

v0.7.2 improves installer servicing, data safety and release delivery while preserving the v0.5/v0.6/v0.7 RCC game and mod compatibility contract.

## Fixes

- Windows Setup recognizes an existing installation and hands Update, Modify and Uninstall to its Maintenance Tool before the occupied directory check. The application component is selected by default, the “You are installing” summary is populated, and optional shortcut controls are guarded when a page has not been created.
- Developer Lab stores an API key in the operating system credential store only after opt-in. Restored keys are verified again; logging out cancels pending responses. Failed keychain writes do not fall back to plaintext.
- Creating a save slot no longer overwrites an existing slot. Nested JavaScript snapshot values are normalized before serialization.
- Catalog, update and developer responses have byte and time limits; malformed catalog URLs are rejected.
- Android packages require signing credentials and include checked OpenSSL libraries per ABI. The build validates packaged native libraries and 16 KiB alignment.
- The backend companion tightens HTTPS and proxy handling, limits upstream and request sizes, checks archives and uses short-lived developer sessions. Deploy the companion separately with its migration and installation checks.

## Updates and downloads

Windows Setup installations use the bundled Maintenance Tool and a Windows QtIFW repository for their CPU variant. Other packages receive update notices and backend download links; install the new package using the platform's normal procedure. The `updates` branch stores QtIFW payloads for Windows only and does not contain every platform's download assets.

The public release has 27 assets: source ZIP; Windows x86_64, x86_64 AVX2 and ARM64 portable ZIPs and Setup EXEs; Linux portable, AppImage and native packages; macOS ZIPs and DMGs; and Android APKs. AABs and unsigned Apple test bundles remain internal workflow artifacts.

## Verification and limits

CI and Build Release Artifacts validated the 27-asset candidate. The Windows installer flow was additionally confirmed by a user after the previous installer fixes. Hardware coverage, Android installation, Apple signing/notarization and the separately deployed backend require their own environment checks; a successful build does not establish those results.

No new game/mod API is required. Save Transfer and the portable `.lmgsave` format remain planned for v0.8.0.

name: LeoMiniGames v0.7.1
body:
# LeoMiniGames v0.7.1

v0.7.1 is a servicing release focused on reliable delivery and updates without changing the game/mod compatibility contract.

## Release and update infrastructure

- Adds a deterministic `release-assets` aggregation step so public GitHub Release files can be uploaded as one validated set.
- Adds a manual, guarded `Publish Release` workflow with exact-commit CI/build checks, duplicate release protection, draft-first publishing and asset verification.
- Fixes draft publication retries by tracking the numeric GitHub release ID; partial drafts are recovered and their asset set is rebuilt safely instead of failing on the published-tag lookup.
- Adds canonical release metadata and a public asset allowlist.
- Adds Qt Installer Framework hybrid installers and GitHub-hosted maintenance repositories for Windows x86_64 and ARM64.
- Adds a Maintenance shortcut for update, repair/modify and uninstall operations.

## Application updates

- Routes update discovery, release metadata, package downloads and Windows QtIFW repository access through `leominigames.younglion.xyz`; GitHub is now a replaceable backend upstream rather than an application dependency.
- Adds a host-level GitHub update service.
- Supports Stable and Preview update channels with SemVer-aware prerelease ordering.
- Installed Windows builds hand update execution to the QtIFW Maintenance Tool.
- Portable/other builds can open the matching public GitHub Release asset or release page.
- Remote metadata is size-bounded and accepted only from HTTPS GitHub endpoints.

## Compatibility

- No new game/mod API is required by v0.7.1.
- Existing v0.5/v0.6/v0.7 package compatibility remains a release requirement.
- Save Transfer and the `.lmgsave` portable format remain planned for the v0.8.0 development line.

name: Version v0.7.0 (First Public Release)
body:
# LeoMiniGames Releases

This document is the canonical release/upgrade guide for LeoMiniGames. It is intentionally more detailed than a short GitHub Release description: it records artifact expectations, compatibility guarantees, migration rules, validation status and known limitations.

## Release policy

LeoMiniGames uses semantic-style `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` versions for the application/runtime contract. Package/API compatibility is handled separately through manifest negotiation so an application release does not automatically invalidate older RCC content.

The GitHub repository does **not** automatically create Releases from tags. `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml` is a manual artifact builder; generated files are intended to be reviewed and then attached to a GitHub Release by the maintainer.

## v0.7.0 — compatibility/security/SDK upgrade

### Release objective

v0.7.0 strengthens the host/runtime boundary without forcing supported v0.5/v0.6 RCC games to be repackaged. The central design is **compatibility through scoped adapters**: old service names and package layouts remain usable while raw host internals are no longer unnecessarily exposed to external game QML.

### Major additions

Developer Lab can validate and session-mount local RCC packages, report API/capability/mount information, export diagnostics and preview device profiles. Modern packages can declare API requirements with explicit `required_capabilities` rather than relying on implicit runtime assumptions.

The game-facing theme and i18n contracts are expanded. Input centralizes physical WASD handling. Save/lifecycle paths use explicit forced persistence at durability boundaries. Audio becomes lazy/capability-aware instead of assuming every platform/backend behaves identically.

### Security and trust changes

Publisher verification is authoritative only when it comes from the trusted YoungLion catalog boundary. A local manifest or custom catalog cannot self-assign Official, Verified or Native/L3 status. Legacy admin-only canonical catalog entries are compatibility-mapped to Official so historical official releases do not incorrectly become Unverified.

External QML receives game-scoped service facades in a separate QML engine. Legacy Settings/Audio/Logger convenience APIs remain available where required, but their access is scoped to the active game/package. Legacy RCC prefix support verifies namespace containment before using a global resource mount.

Native/L3 remains a separate reviewed capability. License choice does not imply Native/L3 permission.

### Backward-compatibility contract

A missing `api_version` remains valid and identifies a legacy package. New RCCs use internal prefix `/` and are mounted at `/mods/<id>`. Historical RCCs that already contain `/mods/<id>` remain accepted when the package is fully contained in that namespace.

Legacy public service names remain available through adapters. Existing game save representations are not rewritten merely because the host upgraded to v0.7.0. Legacy settings can be copied into namespaced storage on read, preserving previous user configuration while isolating future writes.

Compatibility fixtures cover canonical v0.5, legacy-prefix v0.5, v0.6 services, v0.7 modern packages and a deliberately malicious legacy namespace fixture that must be rejected.

### Fixed runtime issues

This release includes fixes for QML syntax/cache-generation errors in Developer Lab, duplicate Qt target finalization, GameAudio URL/string type mismatch, QML network factory API/lifetime handling, missing `GameResources` constructor linkage, installed-content index duplicate iteration, network capability propagation, market model mutation races during downloads, lifecycle force-save gaps, empty state-service paths and inherited QML property shadowing.

Android CI additionally fixes two concrete workflow/build failures: `Haptics.cpp` no longer includes a standalone `QNativeInterface` header when Qt exposes the Android application interface via the Core application header, and Android target `qt-cmake` is invoked through `bash` so a lost archive execute bit does not break armeabi-v7a configuration.

### Platform and CPU coverage

The v0.7.0 GitHub CI configuration covers:

| Platform | CPU/ABI/toolchain | CI operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux Ubuntu 22.04 | x86_64 | build + CTest |
| Linux Ubuntu 24.04 | x86_64 | build + CTest |
| Linux Ubuntu 24.04 | arm64 | build + CTest |
| Windows | x86_64 MSVC 2022 | build + CTest |
| Windows | x86_64 LLVM-MinGW | build + CTest |
| Windows | ARM64 MSVC cross-build | build |
| macOS | arm64 | build + CTest |
| macOS | x86_64 | build + CTest |
| Android | arm64-v8a | APK |
| Android | armeabi-v7a | APK |
| Android | x86_64 | APK |
| Android | x86 | APK |
| iOS Simulator | x86_64 | unsigned build |

These are configured CI lanes. A newly added lane is not labelled “physically verified” until its workflow and, where relevant, hardware QA have actually completed.

### Release artifact matrix

The manual Build Release Artifacts workflow is expected to produce:

| Target | Artifact names/purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Source | `LeoMiniGames-v0.7.0-Source.zip` + SHA-256 |
| Windows x86_64 | portable ZIP + QtIFW Setup EXE |
| Windows ARM64 | portable ZIP + QtIFW Setup EXE |
| Linux x86_64 | runtime tar.gz + AppImage |
| Linux ARM64 | runtime tar.gz + AppImage |
| macOS arm64 | deployed ZIP + DMG |
| macOS x86_64 | deployed ZIP + DMG |
| Android arm64-v8a | signed APK + signed AAB lane |
| Android armeabi-v7a | signed APK |
| Android x86_64 | signed APK |
| Android x86 | signed APK |
| iOS Simulator x86_64 | unsigned test ZIP |

### Windows installation

The portable ZIP is deployed with `windeployqt`. The Qt Installer Framework installer includes the same staged application payload. The main component is marked `ForcedInstallation` and `Essential` so an installer build cannot intentionally present only the Maintenance Tool as the installed product.

Windows artifacts are not claimed to be Authenticode-signed unless a signing certificate/signing stage has actually been configured.

### Linux installation

The portable archive and AppImage derive from a `linuxdeploy` AppDir that contains the application, Qt runtime dependencies, desktop entry and icon. x86_64 and ARM64 use architecture-matching AppImage tooling.

### macOS installation

`macdeployqt` stages the application before ZIP/DMG creation. The current workflow does not pretend to provide Developer ID signing or notarization without Apple credentials. Unsigned artifacts are appropriate for CI/testing, not a substitute for a notarized public macOS distribution policy.

### Android installation and signing

Release APKs use the maintainer-provided GitHub Actions keystore secrets. The keystore itself is never committed. Configured ABIs are `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64` and `x86`.

To preserve Android update compatibility, continue using the correct established upload/distribution key for the same application ID. A differently signed APK may not be accepted as an update over an existing installation.

The current AAB lane is explicitly arm64-v8a. A future multi-ABI AAB should use Qt's CMake multi-ABI support after all corresponding Qt Android kits are installed and verified; v0.7.0 does not falsely label a single-ABI bundle as universal.

### iOS status

CI produces unsigned arm64 device builds and x86_64 simulator archives for both iOS and iPadOS. These are developer/test artifacts. Device IPA/App Store distribution requires Apple signing/provisioning and is not claimed by this workflow.

### Source-available / F-Droid transition

Starting with the source-available licensing transition, the LeoMiniGames host uses `LicenseRef-LMG-SAPEL-1.0`. This license restricts redistribution and therefore current/future source-available editions must not be represented as eligible for the official F-Droid main repository.

The previous F-Droid submission scaffold has been removed. The tracker-free build intent remains available as the neutral **privacy build** profile (`LEOMINIGAMES_PRIVACY_BUILD` / `tools/privacy_clean_build.sh`). A YoungLion-controlled Android repository can be operated separately subject to signing, Qt/LGPL and other third-party obligations. See `docs/F_DROID_TRANSITION.md`.

### Qt version policy

`CMakeLists.txt` retains Qt 6.5 as the minimum API floor. Local development may use Qt 6.11.1. GitHub CI currently pins Qt 6.10.2 because that version has been reliably retrievable by the pinned `install-qt-action`/aqt path. This CI pin does not redefine the application's maximum/supported Qt version.

### Validation

Repository validation includes source guard, project consistency, sanity, security audit, i18n coverage/placeholder validation, distribution checks, prebuilt-binary audit and the v0.7 contract validator. Qt-enabled jobs additionally compile and run CTest where target/toolchain semantics allow it.

Static validation is evidence about source/package contracts; it is not equivalent to real device testing. See `BUG_HUNTER_AUDIT.md`, `GAMER_AUDIT.md`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.md`, `BUILD_MATRIX.md` and `COMPATIBILITY_REPORT.md`.

### Upgrade notes for users

Users upgrading from v0.5/v0.6 should not need to reinstall compatible RCC content solely because of the v0.7 API. Existing game state should be preserved by the save compatibility paths. If a third-party package fails to load, diagnostics should be checked for namespace, malformed manifest, unsupported required capability or an actual runtime error rather than assuming all legacy content is unsupported.

### Migration notes for game/mod developers

Existing legacy packages may remain unchanged while they are supported. New development should move to canonical prefix `/`, documented game-scoped host services and explicit `api_version`/`required_capabilities`. Do not put trust assertions such as Official/Verified/native permission in a manifest expecting the host to honor them.

### Known limitations

Translation coverage is not yet 100% across every supported locale; source-English fallback remains intentional. Full native browser-to-app Developer OAuth callback support remains a backend integration dependency. Apple public distribution signing/notarization is not automated. Newly added CI architecture lanes require their first successful GitHub run before being recorded as verified.

## Manual release procedure

1. Ensure `CMakeLists.txt`, Android versionName/versionCode, installer metadata, changelog and release documentation agree.
2. Run CI and resolve all required job failures.
3. Run **Build Release Artifacts** manually with the exact version.
4. Download and inspect the produced artifacts; verify checksums/signatures where applicable.
5. Perform platform smoke tests on the release binaries, especially Windows and Android.
6. Create the GitHub Release manually and attach the reviewed artifacts.
7. Record known limitations rather than hiding skipped signing/device tests.

## Rollback principle

If a v0.7 runtime/security change breaks a legitimate v0.5/v0.6 package, prefer a compatibility adapter/migration/fallback over deleting old package support. Security exceptions must remain scoped: backward compatibility is not a reason to restore global host filesystem/settings/trust access to external QML.

## Older version documentation

Historical notes remain in `V0.5.0_CHANGES.md`, `V0.5.1_CHANGES.md`, `V0.5.2_CHANGES.md`, `V0.6.1_CHANGES.md` and `V0.6.2_CHANGES.md`.

## Section 22 exclusion

The repository intentionally contains **no tag-triggered automatic GitHub Release creation**. Manual artifact generation and manual release publication remain separate operations unless that policy is explicitly changed in a future task.
